## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to build privacy-preserving, low-latency NLP systems for code-switched language (EN/HI) with bias detection, remediation, and governance in enterprise chat environments.

## Key Concepts

- On-device processing for latency and privacy compliance
- Code-switch handling with EN/HI bilingual resources
- Hybrid detection combining lexicon-based rules with a contextual encoder
- Remediation module providing explainable rewrite suggestions
- Drift-aware evaluation and staged rollout with rollback plans

## Implementation Approach

The system employs a two-tier detection strategy. The on-device tier uses a compact bilingual lexicon paired with a lightweight contextual encoder to achieve sub-100ms latency while preserving privacy by processing sensitive data locally. For ambiguous cases, cloud inference leverages a distilled multilingual model to improve accuracy. The remediation module generates neutral rewrite suggestions with confidence scores, enabling users to self-correct flagged content. High-severity cases automatically escalate to compliance review via the governance gate. Continuous drift-aware evaluation monitors model performance, triggering automated rollback if latency or accuracy degrades beyond defined thresholds.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design lightweight, privacy-conscious NLP with practical constraints.

- Text normalization: emoji/slang handling
- Lightweight bilingual features; on-device constraints
- Hybrid rule+ML approach; latency and privacy trade-offs

## Code Example
```python
import re
EMOJI_MAP = {":)": "smile"}
def normalize(text):
  for k,v in EMOJI_MAP.items():
    text = text.replace(k, v)
  text = re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", "", text)
  return text.lower()
```

This question probes end-to-end design for live, multilingual misinformation detection with tight latency constraints, retrieval-based evidence, and comprehensive auditability.

## Key Concepts
- Streaming NLP and ASR
- Language detection and on-the-fly translation
- Retrieval-Augmented Detection (RAG) and evidence provenance
- Privacy, auditing, drift monitoring, explainability

## Code Example
```python
# Pseudo-structure of streaming pipeline
def process_utterance(utterance):
    text = asr(utterance.audio)
    lang = detect_language(text)
    translated = translate(text, target_lang='en')
    claims = extract_claims(translated)
    evidence = retrieve_evidence(claims)
    scores = compute_confidence(claims, evidence)
    log_interaction(utterance, claims, evidence, scores)
    return claims, evidence, scores
```

## Design Considerations
- **Latency**: Parallel processing, optimized embeddings, and efficient retrieval ensure sub-200ms response
- **Accuracy**: Multilingual ASR quality impacts downstream performance; use ensemble models for language detection
- **Scalability**: Microservices architecture with horizontal scaling for high-throughput scenarios
- **Privacy**: Optional content redaction, user consent mechanisms, and GDPR-compliant data handling
- **Monitoring**: Real-time drift detection on model performance and automated model retraining triggers
